name: Supersets

card.summary: Back-to-back exercises with little rest that shorten workouts and keep training volume, helping people build muscle in less time.
card.note: Metabolically demanding; fatigue can affect performance on the second exercise.

quick.overview:
A superset is two exercises performed one after the other with little or no rest in between. It helps someone build a better physique by fitting the same amount of training into a shorter session, so more people can train consistently.

Reviews and trials report that supersets can roughly halve session length while maintaining training volume, and one meta-analysis of 19 studies and 313 participants compared them with traditional sets across mechanical, metabolic and perceptual outcomes.
quick.how: Common forms pair opposing muscles (biceps and triceps, chest and back), reciprocal pairs, or whole-body exercises. A T Nation member describes alternating one triceps set and one biceps set with hardly any rest, three rounds.
quick.risks: Low risk in general. Supersets are metabolically demanding and the perceived effort is higher; the second exercise can feel harder.

lead: A superset is a training method in which two or more exercises are performed consecutively with short rest intervals between them. [3]

People use supersets to fit more work into a session. Reviews report that supersets, drop sets and rest-pause training can roughly halve training time compared with traditional training while maintaining training volume, which matters for building muscle when time is the barrier. [2][4]
Variants include agonist-antagonist pairs, similar-biomechanics pairs, and alternating pairs, which a 2025 meta-analysis of 19 studies analysed separately. [3]

chain: Pair two exercises back to back
Same training volume in a shorter session
Easier to train consistently and build muscle
angle.text: Supersets save time, which lets lifters hit enough weekly volume to grow muscle. Some forum users use them for bicep-and-tricep pump sessions.

paras: Superset training involves two or more consecutive sets of different exercises with short rest. Applications include agonist-antagonist paired sets, reciprocal supersets and total-body supersets. [4]
On T Nation, a member asked whether he should rest more after supersetting biceps and triceps with minimal rest in three rounds, inviting others' views on supersets. [5]

A 2019 systematic review of 30 articles on advanced resistance-training techniques found that agonist-antagonist and upper-lower supersets may provide an advantage in time efficiency. [1] A 2021 narrative review reported that supersets, drop sets and rest-pause training roughly halve training time while maintaining volume. [2]

A 2025 systematic review and meta-analysis of 19 studies with 313 participants compared supersets with traditional sets. [3] A 2025 narrative review notes that supersets cut session duration by about 50% and that the literature is heterogeneous. [4]

A 2024 randomised trial compared supersets with traditional sets in whole-body multi-joint training, noting that supersets nearly halve session duration but are metabolically demanding. [6] A 2017 randomised trial examined muscle damage and activity during supersets in active men. [7]
